To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there is a strong relationship between the length of a query and the number of documents retrieved; (ii) there is a weak relationship between the number of terms in the query and the number retrieved; and (iii) there is no relationship between the frequency of terms in the collection and the number retrieved.

the problem of choosing a search strategy for a document retrieval system.

, for the best-match document retrieval systems considered in this paper, there is no evidence that any particular search strategy is superior to another for all queries.
there is no evidence that the use of statistical information about queries will improve retrieval effectiveness in best-match systems.
the statistical characteristics of queries do not appear to provide a good basis on which to make decisions about the choice of search strategy in best-match document-retrieval applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of search strategy should depend on the nature of the document collection and the nature of the user's query.
, while the use of search strategies is an important part of document retrieval, the choice of strategy for a particular query is not a simple matter.

the selection of search strategy should be based on the characteristics of the collection, rather than the query, and that the selection should be done at the collection-building stage.
